scenario_summary: Customer is requesting a refund for a service canceled 34 days ago, which is outside the standard 30-day refund window.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Todd Anderson and I'm 64. I'm trying to get a refund for a service I canceled 34 days ago. I know your refund policy is usually 30 days, but I was traveling and only just saw the charge — I didn't realize it had gone through until now. Is there anything you can do?
Okay, Todd. Can you provide the account number or the email address associated with the account so I can look this up?
Sure, the email is todd.anderson@email.com and the account number is 884920.
Thanks. I see the account. You said you canceled 34 days ago, but our policy is strictly 30 days. Why didn't you check your email sooner?
As I mentioned, I was traveling abroad and didn't have consistent access to my inbox. I'm hoping you can make an exception given that I've been a loyal customer for years.
Yeah, I don't know. I'm not really supposed to override the system for this. I'll just go ahead and escalate this to the billing department since I can't do anything about it.
Oh, I was hoping to get this resolved today. Is there no supervisor or manager who can authorize a refund for a few days past the deadline?
I already told you, I'm sending it to the specialists. They'll get back to you in 3-5 business days. Is there anything else?

escalation_reason: Agent failed to utilize discretionary authority for a minor policy exception and instead offloaded the request to the billing department.

judge_scores.justification: The agent displayed a curt and dismissive tone, even questioning the customer's explanation for their delay rather than showing empathy. Furthermore, the agent unnecessarily escalated a minor policy exception request instead of exercising available discretion or attempting to resolve it directly.
